_comment: Contacts: none. Both lids are clearance fits -- the pick lid floats 0.2mm above its plane and the fill lid 0.15mm above its seat -- so both report as NEAR MISS, which is correct. Modelling either as a coplanar resting contact is what made FCL report 66.9mm of penetration on a pair whose real boolean overlap measured 0.000 mm3. Motion (revision 10 review, F1): neither lid is hinged, but the PICK LID is REMOVED, and 'nothing moves' was how a lid with a stop face that jammed on removal (and, before that, no retention at all) went unchecked. Three removal motions are swept: tilting about the back edge (lifting by the front notches, or hinging on from the back), a straight lift, and a lift along the plane's normal. The retention in the OTHER direction (down-slope slide must be stopped) is a contact, not a clearance, and is checked by probes/lid_retention.py with exact boolean overlaps. The two lifts are swept 0-12 mm (the lug is clear of the stop face after 7 mm of lift); a straight lift past about 24 mm would meet the fill lid's pull lip, which the body-only probe does not include, and nobody lifts that far straight: past 7 mm the lid is free to move forward.
